Note the initial review does not use this facade (`process_inbox_pr_review` is the receiver leg, tasks.py docstring 160-163), so only later re-reviews are affected, and the failure is fail-closed (a missed review, never a wrong-tenant binding).

votes.refutation: Attempted refutations: (1) "Two teams cannot have runs for the same repository" - false, GitHub Integration uniqueness includes team and the manager explicitly resolves one installation across a user's teams; Task.repository is an unconstrained string. (2) "A foreign-team run can never carry this PR URL" - false, the tasks webhook backstop binds output.pr_url through the same team-unscoped branch match, and runs can be created on any checkout branch; run-output writes also accept any pr_url. (3) "The docstring says team scoping is enforced here" - it is enforced only in the fail-closed direction (never returns another tenant's run); it does not guarantee the requested team's qualifying run is found, which is exactly the gap. (4) "Blast radius is a wrong approval" - refuted: the caller fails closed to ordinary bot handling, so the harm is a missed self-driving re-review, which is why this is should_fix rather than must_fix.

votes.evidence:
Code behavior confirmed: products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:504 calls find_task_run(pr_url, branch, repository) with no team filter, then api.py:505 rejects runs whose team_id differs. find_task_run (products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:39-57) filters output__pr_url + task__repository__iexact and orders terminal_rank, -created_at; the branch legs (webhooks.py:65-86) also carry no team filter. So the ordering-before-scoping the finding describes does exist.

Why the premise has no reachable trigger: a GitHub PR URL identifies exactly one PR, and only the run that opened it records it in output.pr_url (agent-side detection, or the webhook backstop at webhooks.py:184-185 / _record_run_pr_url, which binds one run per delivery and only for internal-branch PRs). For a second team to hold a run with the same pr_url on the same repository, a user in that other team would have to hand-edit output.pr_url to point at another tenant's PR (load_pr_urls.py:26 notes output.pr_url is user-writable). Absent that tampering, the newest matching run is the only matching run. Self-driving head branches are per-run generated names, so the branch leg cannot collide across teams either.

Failure direction is fail-closed: even in the tampered case the facade returns None and the carve-out at products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:201 falls back to treating the PR as an ordinary bot PR (no self-driving review starts). No cross-tenant data is returned; the docstring's promise at api.py:492-494 ("a run belonging to any other team returns None") holds.

Existing coverage: products/tasks/backend/tests/test_webhooks.py:1284-1316 (TestFindSignalImplementationRun.test_non_qualifying_runs_return_none, case "other_team") asserts the fail-closed team check; test_webhooks.py:878-908 cover the pr_url leg's terminal/resume preference and repository scoping. The production GitHub webhook path itself (webhooks.py:159) already resolves runs without a team filter, so the facade mirrors the established lookup contract rather than diverging from it.
votes.refutation: The claim needs two teams to own TaskRuns carrying the same output.pr_url for the same repository. A PR URL is minted by GitHub for a single PR and is written to exactly one run (the one that opened it, or the single run the webhook backstop binds). That state is only reachable if a user in a different team manually rewrites their run's output.pr_url to another tenant's PR, and even then the outcome is the safe one: find_signal_implementation_run returns None and the bot PR is reviewed as an ordinary PR instead of getting the self-driving carve-out. The "other_team" parameterized case in test_webhooks.py:1284-1316 already pins the fail-closed behavior. Pushing team_id into find_task_run would be optional hardening against a contrived cross-tenant tampering scenario, not a fix for a reachable defect, and certainly not a must_fix that "prevents legitimate Inbox PR reviews from starting" in normal operation.

votes.evidence:
Code behavior (worktree /Users/woutut/.worktrees/posthog/frozen-75215):
- products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:504-506: `run = find_task_run(pr_url=pr_url, branch=head_branch, repository=repository)` then `if run is None or run.team_id != team_id: return None`. The team check is applied only after a single row has been chosen.
- products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:29-86: `find_task_run` never filters on team. pr_url leg (39-57) filters `output__pr_url` + `task__repository__iexact`, orders non-terminal first then `-created_at`, takes `.first()`. Branch leg (65-75) filters `branch`, `task__repository__iexact`, `state__wizard_head_branch__isnull=True` and calls `.first()` with NO ordering; TaskRun.id is uuid4 (products/tasks/backend/models.py:1075-1076), so which team's row wins there is effectively arbitrary.
- The docstring at api.py:489-494 states the intent: "the signals-origin implementation run that produced this PR ... in the given team" — so a result of None when the given team does have a matching run contradicts the function's own contract.

Reachability in production configuration:
- Multiple teams sharing one GitHub repo in Tasks is explicitly modeled: products/tasks/backend/tests/test_webhooks.py:832-836 creates "Other External Team" with a github integration for the same account and asserts oldest-team-wins resolution. Stamphog config is unique per (installation, repository) (products/stamphog/backend/models.py:67-71), so exactly one team owns the review, but Task.repository is plain per-team text with no such uniqueness.
- A run in another team with the same checkout branch is user-creatable: task/run creation accepts an arbitrary `branch` ("Git branch to checkout in the sandbox", products/tasks/backend/presentation/serializers.py:173-175, 1690-1695, 2199-2204) and `Task.create_and_run` stores it on `TaskRun.branch` (models.py:802). A team-B user checking out the self-driving PR's head branch in the same repo satisfies the branch leg. `output.pr_url` is likewise writable through `set_task_run_output` (products/tasks/backend/presentation/views/api.py:1118) from the agent server.
- Only caller is the webhook carve-out at products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:191-200; on None it returns `_InboxCarveOut()`, so the bot-authored draft self-driving PR falls back to the ordinary path, which skips bot/draft PRs. Consequence: follow-up head-push reviews for the legitimately configured team are silently skipped. Fail-closed direction (no cross-tenant review), no data loss, no security impact.

Existing tests (test_webhooks.py:1265-1310) cover single-team cases and "other_team returns None" but never a same-repo run in a second team alongside a valid run in the requested team, so nothing guards this.
votes.refutation: Attempted refutations: (1) Stamphog's unique (provider, installation_id, repository) constraint means only one team owns the review — but that constrains StamphogRepoConfig, not Tasks' TaskRun/Task.repository, which is per-team and can name the same repo in many teams (the tests themselves model this). (2) The pr_url leg prefers non-terminal/newest, so the original run might usually win — but the self-driving run is typically terminal by the time later webhooks arrive, and the branch leg has no ordering at all with uuid4 pks, so the other team's row can win. (3) Maybe returning None is deliberate fail-closed behavior on ambiguity — the docstring says the function answers for "the given team" and the caller re-checks team_id anyway, so scoping inside the lookup loses nothing and the current shape only creates false negatives. Refutation fails; however the trigger needs a second team with a run on the same branch/PR in the same repo and the outcome is a missed re-review, not a wrong or cross-tenant review, so must_fix is overstated — should_fix.
